questions.question: Identify the sentence that has all comparative forms spelled accurately according to standard inflection rules:

options.text: The junior clerk prepared a redder and biger chart for the courtroom presentation.
The junior clerk prepared a redder and bigger chart for the courtroom presentation.
The junior clerk prepared a reder and bigger chart for the courtroom presentation.
The junior clerk prepared a more red and more big chart for the courtroom presentation.

questions.explanation: 'Red' aur 'big' dono monosyllabic adjectives hain jo single short vowel ke baad single consonant par end hote hain (CVC pattern). Standard inflection rule ke anusaar comparative '-er' lagane se pehle final consonant double ho jata hai: r-e-d-d-e-r aur b-i-g-g-e-r. Option B bilkul accurate hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02: Regular Inflections & CVC Consonant Doubling.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14 Certification

questions.subtopic: Irregular Comparisons: Farther vs Further in Legal Context
questions.question:
Fill in the blanks with the appropriate words:
"The registry is located two kilometers ___ down the road, and the bench directed that no ___ delay would be tolerated."

options.text: further, farther
farther, further
farther, farther
further, further

questions.explanation: Pehle blank mein physical measurable distance ('two kilometers...') hai, isliye strictly 'FARTHER' aayega. Doosre blank mein 'additional / extra delay' (abstract progression) hai, isliye strictly 'FURTHER' aayega. Sequence 'farther, further' (Option B) strictly correct hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03: Irregular Adjectives & Suppletive Grading.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14 Certification

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence containing the grammatical error:
"Following the software update, (A) / the optical character recognition tool (B) / produced more better transcriptions (C) / of historical judicial records. (D)"

options.text: Part A (Following the software update)
Part B (the optical character recognition tool)
Part C (produced more better transcriptions)
Part D (of historical judicial records)

questions.explanation: Part C mein error hai. 'Better' already 'good' ka irregular comparative form hai. Iske sath additional periphrastic marker 'more' lagana double comparative pleonasm hai. Correct expression 'produced better transcriptions' hona chahiye.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Double Comparative & Superlative Ban (Pleonasm).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14 Certification

questions.question:
Select the option that corrects the error in the sentence:
"The newly appointed System Assistant is junior than all other technical officers in the department."

options.text: The newly appointed System Assistant is more junior than all other technical officers in the department.
The newly appointed System Assistant is junior to all other technical officers in the department.
The newly appointed System Assistant is junior from all other technical officers in the department.
The newly appointed System Assistant is most junior than all other technical officers in the department.

questions.explanation: Latin origin ke adjectives (junior, senior, superior, inferior, prior) hamesha preposition 'TO' demand karte hain, 'than' nahi. Isliye 'junior to all other technical officers' (Option B) bilkul correct hai. Option A mein 'more junior than' double error hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06: The Latin Comparative Law: '-OR' Adjectives Take 'TO'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14 Certification

questions.question: Choose the grammatically flawless sentence:

options.text: The administrative clerk prefers updating digital databases than filing manual ledgers.
The administrative clerk prefers updating digital databases to filing manual ledgers.
The administrative clerk prefers updating digital databases more than filing manual ledgers.
The administrative clerk prefers updating digital databases over filing manual ledgers than earlier.

questions.explanation: Verb 'prefer' do verbal actions ko compare karte waqt 'prefer + Gerund (updating) + TO + Gerund (filing)' construction demand karti hai. 'Than' ya 'more than' lagana non-standard syntax hai. Option B strictly compliant hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07: The 'Prefer...To' and 'Preferable To' Law.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14 Certification

questions.question:
Which option rectifies the faulty comparison in the sentence below?
"The digital security architecture of the Principal Seat at Jodhpur is more sophisticated than the Jaipur Bench."

options.text: The digital security architecture of the Principal Seat at Jodhpur is more sophisticated than that of the Jaipur Bench.
The digital security architecture of the Principal Seat at Jodhpur is more sophisticated than those of the Jaipur Bench.
The digital security architecture of the Principal Seat at Jodhpur is more sophisticated then the Jaipur Bench.
The digital security architecture of the Principal Seat at Jodhpur is sophisticated than that of the Jaipur Bench.

questions.explanation: Left side entity 'The digital security architecture' (singular abstract noun) hai. Right side par seedhe 'Jaipur Bench' (court institution) se compare kar diya gaya jo illogical mismatch hai. Singular attribute 'architecture' ke liye demonstrative pronoun 'THAT OF' lagakar balance establish kiya gaya: 'more sophisticated than that of the Jaipur Bench' (Option A).
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Logical Equivalence in Comparisons: 'That of' & 'Those of'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14 Certification

questions.question:
Spot the error part in the following sentence:
"The procedural rules (A) / of the High Court (B) / are far more stringent (C) / than subordinate courts. (D)"

options.text: Part A (The procedural rules)
Part B (of the High Court)
Part C (are far more stringent)
Part D (than subordinate courts)

questions.explanation: Part D mein error hai. 'Procedural rules' (plural noun) ka comparison seedhe 'subordinate courts' se nahi ho sakta; subordinate courts ke procedural rules se hona chahiye. Plural noun ko represent karne ke liye 'than THOSE OF subordinate courts' hona compulsory hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Logical Equivalence in Comparisons: 'That of' & 'Those of'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14 Certification

questions.question: Identify the sentence that correctly excludes the subject from its comparison group:

options.text: Justice Sharma is more learned than any advocate appearing before the court.
Justice Sharma is more learned than any judge on the current High Court roster.
Justice Sharma is more learned than any other judge on the current High Court roster.
Justice Sharma is more learned than all judge on the current High Court roster.

questions.explanation: Justice Sharma khud High Court roster ke ek judge hain. Jab kisi member ko usi ke category ke members se compare kiya jaye, toh subject ko exclude karne ke liye 'OTHER' lagana mandatory hai: 'than ANY OTHER judge' (Option C). Option B mein 'other' missing hone ki wajah se Justice Sharma khud apne aap se compare ho rahe hain.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: Group Self-Exclusion: 'Than Any Other + Singular Noun'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14 Certification

questions.subtopic: 'One of the' Superlative Concord with Relative Clause
questions.question:
Choose the option that maintains flawless subject-verb concord and plural noun agreement:
"This judicial officer is one of the most dedicated ___ on the state examination committee."

options.text: magistrate who has served
magistrates who have served
magistrates who has served
magistrate who have served

questions.explanation: 'One of the + superlative' ke baad hamesha PLURAL noun lagta hai ('magistrates'). Aur relative pronoun 'who' ka antecedent plural noun 'magistrates' hai, isliye relative clause ki verb bhi PLURAL hogi ('who HAVE served'). Dono rules Option B mein bilkul accurate hain.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: The 'One of the' Superlative Concord Formula.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14 Certification

questions.subtopic: Comparing Two Qualities of the Same Entity
questions.question: Select the sentence that accurately compares two distinct qualities possessed by the same individual:

options.text: The defense attorney was cleverer than honest during the cross-examination.
The defense attorney was more clever than honest during the cross-examination.
The defense attorney was more cleverer than honest during the cross-examination.
The defense attorney was clever than honest during the cross-examination.

questions.explanation: Jab do alag logon ka comparison na ho, balki ek hi person ki do alag qualities (clever vs honest) ka comparison ho, toh '-er' form use karna prohibited hai. Rule demands 'MORE + base adjective 1 + than + base adjective 2': 'more clever than honest' (Option B).
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-11: Two Qualities of the Same Entity ('More...Than').
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14 Certification

questions.subtopic: Countable vs Uncountable Concord: Fewer vs Less
questions.question: Which of the following sentences correctly applies countability concord?

options.text: There are less judicial vacancies in the subordinate judiciary this year than last year.
There are fewer judicial vacancies in the subordinate judiciary this year than last year.
The department spent fewer expenditure on hardware procurement this quarter.
The new e-portal resulted in fewer delay during case filing.

questions.explanation: 'Vacancies' plural countable noun hai jise number mein count kiya ja sakta hai, isliye iske pehle strictly 'FEWER' lagta hai ('fewer judicial vacancies' - Option B). 'Expenditure' aur 'delay' uncountable nouns hain jinke sath 'less' lagna chahiye tha, isliye Options C aur D incorrect hain.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14 Certification

questions.question:
Choose the option that correctly completes the correlative comparative structure:
"___ the digital evidence is examined, ___ the probability of uncovering the server intrusion becomes."

options.text: The more thorough, greater
The more thoroughly, the greater
More thoroughly, the greater
The more thoroughly, greater

questions.explanation: Do key rules apply ho rahe hain: (1) Passive verb 'is examined' ke manner ko modify karne ke liye adverb 'thoroughly' (comparative: 'more thoroughly') chahiye; (2) Correlative structure mein dono clauses ke pehle definite article 'THE' aana mandatory hai: 'THE more thoroughly..., THE greater...' (Option B).
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-12: Parallel Progression: 'The More..., The More...'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14 Certification

questions.subtopic: Sentence Transformation: Apex Superlative to Positive
questions.question:
Select the correct Positive degree transformation that preserves the exact meaning of:
"The Supreme Court is the highest judicial authority in India."

options.text: Very few judicial authorities in India are as high as the Supreme Court.
No other judicial authority in India is as high as the Supreme Court.
The Supreme Court is as high as any other judicial authority in India.
No other judicial authorities in India are as high as the Supreme Court.

questions.explanation: Original sentence 'the highest' (unique apex) declare kar raha hai. Unique apex ko Positive degree mein transform karne ke liye formula hai: 'NO OTHER + Singular Noun (judicial authority) + is as high as + the Supreme Court'. 'Very few' subset ke liye hota hai aur Option D mein 'authorities' plural noun discord hai. Isliye Option B strictly correct hai.
questions.ruleReference: Section 10: Sentence Transformation Across Degrees While Preserving Meaning.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14 Certification

questions.subtopic: Sentence Transformation: Subset 'One of the' to Comparative
questions.question:
Transform the following sentence into Comparative degree without altering its meaning:
"Dr. Ambedkar was one of the greatest constitutional jurists of the modern world."

options.text: Dr. Ambedkar was greater than any other constitutional jurist of the modern world.
Dr. Ambedkar was greater than most other constitutional jurists of the modern world.
Dr. Ambedkar was not greater than most other constitutional jurists of the modern world.
No other constitutional jurist was greater than Dr. Ambedkar.

questions.explanation: Original sentence 'one of the greatest' (subset bracket) hai. 'One of the' ka Comparative transformation 'than MOST OTHER + plural noun' hota hai: 'greater than most other constitutional jurists' (Option B). 'Than any other' unique apex ke liye hota hai jo original meaning ko alter kar deta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Section 10: Sentence Transformation Across Degrees While Preserving Meaning.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14 Certification

questions.question: Choose the sentence that is completely free from grammatical, logical, and concord errors:

options.text: The judicial speed of the e-court portal is more faster than traditional court benches.
The judicial speed of the e-court portal is faster than that of traditional court benches.
The judicial speed of the e-court portal is faster than those of traditional court benches.
The judicial speed of the e-court portal is more fast than that of traditional court benches.

questions.explanation: Option B mein sabhi grammatical filters perfectly satisfied hain: (1) Adjective 'fast' ka comparative 'faster' hai bina kisi redundant 'more' ke (eliminating A & D); (2) Left-hand entity singular noun 'speed' hai, isliye logical equivalence maintain karne ke liye singular pronoun 'THAT OF' use hua hai (eliminating C jo plural 'those of' use kar raha hai). Isliye Option B 100% defect-free hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14 Certification
